source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Repository follows Hebrew labels: 4:17 and 5:1–19 retained, without conversion to common English numbering.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Repeat absent comfort and locate power with oppressors.
verses.before: Again I saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And look: the tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; power is in the hand of their oppressors, and they have no comforter.
verses.after: I turned again to look at all the oppression under the sun. Look at the tears of the oppressed— no one comforts them. Power lies with their oppressors, and no one comforts them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again I saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun. And look: the tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter; power is in the hand of their oppressors, and they have no comforter.

verses.rationale: Keep Qohelet’s disturbing comparative judgment in his voice.
verses.before: So I praised the dead, who have already died, more than the living, who are still alive.
verses.after: So I called the dead, who have already died, more fortunate than the living, who are still alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I praised the dead, who have already died, more than the living, who are still alive.

verses.rationale: Retain unborn alternative and evil’s visibility.
verses.before: Better than both is the one who has not yet been— who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.after: Better off than either is the one not yet born, who has not seen the evil done under the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better than both is the one who has not yet been— who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

verses.rationale: Render envy as rivalry while keeping sweeping observation.
verses.before: I saw all toil and every skill in work: it is the envy of one person for another. This too is vapor and a pursuit of wind.
verses.after: I saw that all hard work and every skillful achievement spring from rivalry between neighbors. This too is breath, herding the wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I saw all toil and every skill in work: it is the envy of one person for another. This too is vapor and a pursuit of wind.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily image of self-consuming idleness.
verses.before: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
verses.after: The fool folds his hands and eats away his own flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.

verses.rationale: Preserve one/two hand contrast and recurring wind image.
verses.before: Better one handful with rest than two handfuls with toil and a pursuit of wind.
verses.after: Better a single handful with rest than two full hands of hard work and herding the wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better one handful with rest than two handfuls with toil and a pursuit of wind.

verses.rationale: Introduce the isolated worker as another hevel observation.
verses.before: Again I saw vapor under the sun:
verses.after: Again I turned and saw breath under the sun:
verses.tsw_comparator: Again I saw vapor under the sun:

verses.rationale: Retain male kin terms, singular eye read form, and self-question.
verses.before: There is one person, and no second; they have neither son nor brother, yet there is no end to all their toil, and their eyes are never satisfied with wealth. “For whom, then, am I toiling and depriving myself of good?” This too is vapor and an evil task.
verses.after: a man alone, with no companion, without son or brother. There is no end to his work, yet his eye is never satisfied with wealth. “For whom am I working, denying myself enjoyment?” This too is breath—a miserable task.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is one person, and no second; they have neither son nor brother, yet there is no end to all their toil, and their eyes are never satisfied with wealth. “For whom, then, am I toiling and depriving myself of good?” This too is vapor and an evil task.

verses.rationale: Link advantage to shared labor’s return.
verses.before: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.
verses.after: Two are better off than one, because their work brings them a good return.
verses.tsw_comparator: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.

verses.rationale: Keep conditional fall and solitary counterpart.
verses.before: For if they fall, one will raise up the other. But woe to the one who falls and has no second to raise them up.
verses.after: If they fall, one can lift the other up. But how miserable to fall alone, with no one to help you up!
verses.tsw_comparator: For if they fall, one will raise up the other. But woe to the one who falls and has no second to raise them up.

verses.rationale: Retain physical warmth without narrowing relationship.
verses.before: Again, if two lie down together, they are warm; but how can one be warm alone?
verses.after: And if two lie down together, they keep warm. How can one person keep warm alone?
verses.tsw_comparator: Again, if two lie down together, they are warm; but how can one be warm alone?

verses.rationale: Keep numerical movement from one to two to three.
verses.before: If someone overpowers one, two can stand against that person. And a threefold cord is not quickly torn apart.
verses.after: Someone may overpower one person, but two can stand against the attacker. A cord of three strands does not quickly break.
verses.tsw_comparator: If someone overpowers one, two can stand against that person. And a threefold cord is not quickly torn apart.

verses.rationale: Retain age, poverty, wisdom, and refusal to heed warning.
verses.before: Better a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to take warning.
verses.after: Better a poor, wise youth than an old, foolish king who no longer takes advice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to take warning.

verses.rationale: Clarify youth as subject while preserving prison and low birth.
verses.before: For from a prison house he came out to reign, though even in his kingdom he was born poor.
verses.after: The youth may come out of prison to reign, even though he was born poor in that kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: For from a prison house he came out to reign, though even in his kingdom he was born poor.

verses.rationale: Keep second youth and succession without inventing identities.
verses.before: I saw all the living who walk under the sun with the second youth who stands in his place.
verses.after: I saw all the living who walk under the sun side with the second youth, who would take his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw all the living who walk under the sun with the second youth who stands in his place.

verses.rationale: Retain changing popular favor and distinct wind noun.
verses.before: There was no end to all the people, to everyone who were before them. Yet people who come later will not rejoice in him. Surely this too is vapor and a pursuit of wind.
verses.after: There was no end to all the people he led. Yet those who come later will not delight in him either. This too is breath, a pursuit of wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was no end to all the people, to all who were before them. Yet those who come later will not rejoice in him. Surely this too is vapor and a pursuit of wind.

verses.rationale: Preserve repository4:17 label; hearing contrasts with foolish sacrifice.
verses.before: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. To draw near in order to listen is better than for fools to offer sacrifice, for they do not know that they are doing evil.
verses.after: Watch your step when you go to God’s house. Draw near to listen, rather than offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know they are doing wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. To draw near in order to listen is better than for fools to offer sacrifice, for they do not know that they are doing evil.

verses.rationale: Keep mouth/heart distinction and heaven/earth rationale.
verses.before: Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart be quick to bring forth a word before God. For God is in heaven and you are on earth; therefore let your words be few.
verses.after: Do not let your mouth rush ahead, or your heart hurry to speak before God. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so keep your words few.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart be quick to bring forth a word before God. For God is in heaven and you are on earth; therefore let your words be few.

verses.rationale: Preserve parallel abundance of business and speech.
verses.before: For a dream comes through much activity, and a fool’s voice through many words.
verses.after: Dreams come with much preoccupation; a fool’s voice comes with many words.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a dream comes through much activity, and a fool’s voice through many words.

verses.rationale: Keep obligation and repeated pay/vow language.
verses.before: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in paying it, for he takes no pleasure in fools. What you vow, pay.
verses.after: When you make a vow to God, do not delay paying it. He takes no pleasure in fools. Pay what you vow.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in paying it, for he takes no pleasure in fools. What you vow, pay.

verses.rationale: Preserve simple negative comparison.
verses.before: Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.
verses.after: Better not to vow than to vow and leave it unpaid.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.

verses.rationale: Keep body, messenger ambiguity, and concrete consequences.
verses.before: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the messenger, “It was an error.” Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
verses.after: Do not let your mouth lead your body into sin. Do not tell the messenger, “It was a mistake.” Why make God angry at your voice and let him destroy the work of your hands?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the messenger, “It was an error.” Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?

verses.rationale: Render compressed accumulation with hevel retained.
verses.before: For in an abundance of dreams, and vapors, and many words—fear God.
verses.after: With many dreams come much breath and many words. Fear God instead.
verses.tsw_comparator: For in an abundance of dreams, and vapors, and many words—fear God.

verses.rationale: Preserve layered officials without declaring their oversight benevolent.
verses.before: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the robbery of justice and righteousness in a province, do not be astonished at the matter. For one high official watches over another high official, and higher ones are over them.
verses.after: If you see the poor oppressed and justice and righteousness stolen in a province, do not be astonished: one high official watches another, with still higher officials above them.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you see the oppression of the poor, and the robbery of justice and righteousness in a province, do not be astonished at the matter. For one high official watches over another high official, and higher ones are over them.

verses.rationale: Give readable agricultural relation, documenting difficult syntax.
verses.before: Yet the advantage of a land is in everything: a king is served by a field.
verses.after: The land’s yield benefits everyone; even a king depends on cultivated fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the advantage of a land is in everything: a king is served by a field.

verses.rationale: Retain silver repetition and dissatisfaction parallel.
verses.before: Whoever loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor whoever loves abundance with income. This too is vapor.
verses.after: A lover of silver never has enough silver; a lover of wealth never has enough income. This too is breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor whoever loves abundance with income. This too is vapor.

verses.rationale: Keep increase and visual-only benefit question.
verses.before: When good things increase, people who consume them increase; and what advantage is there to their owners except to look on with their eyes?
verses.after: As goods multiply, so do the people who consume them. What benefit do their owners gain, beyond looking at them?
verses.tsw_comparator: When good things increase, those who consume them increase; and what advantage is there to their owners except to look on with their eyes?

verses.rationale: Retain eating quantities and satiation’s ironic cost.
verses.before: Sweet is the sleep of one who works, whether they eat little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not let them sleep.
verses.after: A laborer sleeps sweetly, whether the meal is small or large. But a rich person’s full stomach will not let him sleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sweet is the sleep of one who works, whether they eat little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not let them sleep.

verses.rationale: Keep hoarded wealth as harm to owner.
verses.before: There is a grievous evil that I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to their harm.
verses.after: I have seen a grievous evil under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his own hurt.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a grievous evil that I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to their harm.

verses.rationale: Preserve son and empty-handed loss.
verses.before: That wealth is lost through a bad venture, and they father a child, but there is nothing in their hand.
verses.after: That wealth is lost in a bad venture. He has a son, but nothing remains in his hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: That wealth is lost through a bad venture, and they father a child, but there is nothing in their hand.

verses.rationale: Repeat coming/leaving and retain womb/hand imagery.
verses.before: As they came forth from their mother’s womb, naked they will return, going as they came; and from their labor they will carry nothing away in their hand.
verses.after: Naked he came from his mother’s womb, and naked he will leave, just as he came. Nothing from his hard work can he carry away in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: As they came forth from their mother’s womb, naked they will return, going as they came; and from their labor they will carry nothing away in their hand.

verses.rationale: Keep wind as recipient of futile work.
verses.before: This also is a grievous evil: entirely as they came, so they go. What profit is there for them in laboring for the wind?
verses.after: This too is a grievous evil: he goes exactly as he came. What does he gain from working for the wind?
verses.tsw_comparator: This also is a grievous evil: entirely as they came, so they go. What profit is there for them in laboring for the wind?

verses.rationale: Preserve dark meals and all three afflictions.
verses.before: Indeed, all their days they eat in darkness, with much vexation, sickness, and anger.
verses.after: All his days he eats in darkness, with much vexation, sickness, and anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, all their days they eat in darkness, with much vexation, sickness, and anger.

verses.rationale: Maintain gift, portion, and limited days without universal promise.
verses.before: Look: what I have seen to be good and fitting is to eat and drink and see good in all one’s labor under the sun, during the few days of one’s life that God has given; for this is one’s portion.
verses.after: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat, drink, and enjoy the good in all the work one does under the sun, during the few days of life God gives. This is one’s portion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look: what I have seen to be good and fitting is to eat and drink and see good in all one’s labor under the sun, during the few days of one’s life that God has given; for this is one’s portion.

verses.rationale: Distinguish possession from capacity to enjoy it.
verses.before: Also, every person to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and whom he has enabled to eat from them, to carry their portion, and to rejoice in their labor—this is God’s gift.
verses.after: When God gives someone wealth and possessions, and the power to enjoy them, to receive a portion and delight in work, that is God’s gift.
verses.tsw_comparator: Also, every person to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and whom he has enabled to eat from them, to carry their portion, and to rejoice in their labor—this is God’s gift.

verses.rationale: Render occupation reading of difficult answering verb with note.
verses.before: For they will not remember much the days of their life, because God answers with the joy of their heart.
verses.after: Such a person does not dwell much on life’s days, because God keeps the heart occupied with joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they will not remember much the days of their life, because God answers with the joy of their heart.

verses.rationale: Introduce widespread burden without softening evil.
verses.before: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon humanity:
verses.after: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily on humanity:
verses.tsw_comparator: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon humanity:

verses.rationale: Keep God as agent of both giving and withholding.
verses.before: a person to whom God gives wealth, possessions, and honor, lacking nothing for their appetite of all that they desire, yet God does not empower them to enjoy it; rather, a stranger enjoys it. This is vapor and a grievous sickness.
verses.after: God gives a man wealth, possessions, and honor—nothing he desires is lacking—but God does not give him power to enjoy them. A stranger enjoys them instead. This is breath, a grievous affliction.
verses.tsw_comparator: a person to whom God gives wealth, possessions, and honor, lacking nothing for their appetite of all that they desire, yet God does not empower them to enjoy it; rather, a stranger enjoys it. This is vapor and a grievous sickness.

verses.rationale: Preserve hundred, denied burial, and painful comparison.
verses.before: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years—however many the days of his years may be—but his appetite is not satisfied with good things, and he receives no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
verses.after: A man might father a hundred children and live many years. Yet however many his days, if he has no satisfaction in life’s good things and not even a burial, I say a stillborn child is better off than he is.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years—however many the days of his years may be—but his appetite is not satisfied with good things, and he receives no burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

verses.rationale: Keep stillborn child’s hidden name and hevel image.
verses.before: For it comes in vapor and goes away in darkness, and its name is covered in darkness.
verses.after: It comes in breath and goes into darkness; in darkness its name is hidden.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it comes in vapor and goes away in darkness, and its name is covered in darkness.

verses.rationale: Retain comparison of rest, not an added afterlife claim.
verses.before: Though it has not seen the sun or known anything, it has more rest than he.
verses.after: Though it has never seen the sun or known anything, it has more rest than that man.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though it has not seen the sun or known anything, it has more rest than he.

verses.rationale: Keep two thousand years and unresolved destination.
verses.before: Even if he lives twice a thousand years but sees no good thing—do not all go to one place?
verses.after: Even if he lived a thousand years twice over but never enjoyed life’s good, do not all go to the same place?
verses.tsw_comparator: Even if he lives twice a thousand years but sees no good thing—do not all go to one place?

verses.rationale: Preserve mouth/appetite contrast.
verses.before: All human labor is for the mouth, yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.after: All human work is for the mouth, yet the appetite is never filled.
verses.tsw_comparator: All human labor is for the mouth, yet the appetite is not filled.

verses.rationale: Keep two questions and social competence of poor person.
verses.before: For what advantage does the wise have over the fool? What advantage does the poor person have, knowing how to conduct themselves before the living?
verses.after: What advantage does the wise person have over the fool? What advantage has a poor person who knows how to conduct himself among the living?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what advantage does the wise have over the fool? What advantage does the poor person have, knowing how to conduct themselves before the living?

verses.rationale: Keep sight versus wandering desire, not modern possession proverb.
verses.before: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite. This too is vapor and a chasing after wind.
verses.after: Better what the eyes can see than the appetite’s wandering. This too is breath, herding the wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the appetite. This too is vapor and a chasing after wind.

verses.rationale: Preserve prior naming and unequal contest without supplying God’s name.
verses.before: Whatever has been already has its name, and it is known that it is human; nor can anyone contend with one stronger than they are.
verses.after: Whatever exists has already been named. What a human is has been made known; no one can contend with someone stronger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever has been already has its name, and it is known that it is human; nor can anyone contend with one stronger than they are.

verses.rationale: Keep words/hevel relation and rhetorical question.
verses.before: For there are many words that increase vapor. What advantage is there for anyone?
verses.after: The more words, the more breath. What advantage is that to anyone?
verses.tsw_comparator: For there are many words that increase vapor. What advantage is there for anyone?

verses.rationale: Retain repeated uncertainty, breath, shadow, and afterlife temporal question.
verses.before: For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the numbered days of their vaporous life, which they spend like a shadow? For who can tell a person what will be after them under the sun?
verses.after: Who knows what is good for a person in life, through the few days of a breathlike life spent like a shadow? Who can tell anyone what will happen under the sun after they are gone?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the numbered days of their vaporous life, which they spend like a shadow? For who can tell a person what will be after them under the sun?

verses.rationale: Keep name/oil comparison and unsettling death/birth claim.
verses.before: A good name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.
verses.after: A good name is better than fine oil, and the day of death than the day of birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: A good name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

verses.rationale: Make common end clear while keeping house imagery.
verses.before: Better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for this is the end of every human being, and the living should take it to heart.
verses.after: Better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, for death is everyone’s end, and the living should take it to heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for this is the end of every human being, and the living should take it to heart.

verses.rationale: Preserve face/heart contrast without promising happiness.
verses.before: Sorrow is better than laughter, for through a sad face the heart is made glad.
verses.after: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad face can make the heart better.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sorrow is better than laughter, for through a sad face the heart is made glad.

verses.rationale: Retain location metaphor and plural classes.
verses.before: The heart of the wise is in a house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in a house of joy.
verses.after: The wise have their hearts in the house of mourning; fools have theirs in the house of pleasure.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the wise is in a house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in a house of joy.

verses.rationale: Keep rebuke/song auditory contrast.
verses.before: Better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for one to hear the song of fools.
verses.after: Better to hear a wise person’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better to hear the rebuke of the wise than for one to hear the song of fools.

verses.rationale: Preserve thorns/pot sound image and refrain.
verses.before: For like the crackling of thorns under a pot is the laughter of a fool; this too is vapor.
verses.after: Like thorns crackling under a pot, so is a fool’s laughter. This too is breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: For like the crackling of thorns under a pot is the laughter of a fool; this too is vapor.

verses.rationale: Keep oppression and corrupting gift without restricting cause.
verses.before: For oppression drives the wise into madness, and a bribe destroys the heart.
verses.after: Oppression can drive the wise mad, and a bribe destroys the heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: For oppression drives the wise into madness, and a bribe destroys the heart.

verses.rationale: Retain paired comparisons and spirit imagery.
verses.before: Better is the end of a matter than its beginning; better is patience than pride.
verses.after: Better the end of a matter than its beginning; better a patient spirit than a proud one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Better is the end of a matter than its beginning; better is patience than pride.

verses.rationale: Keep lap as anger’s resting place.
verses.before: Do not be quick in your spirit to become angry, for anger rests in the lap of fools.
verses.after: Do not be quick in spirit to anger, for anger settles in a fool’s lap.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be quick in your spirit to become angry, for anger rests in the lap of fools.

verses.rationale: Retain critique of question rather than claim about all history.
verses.before: Do not say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For it is not from wisdom that you ask this.
verses.after: Do not ask, “Why were the old days better than these?” Wisdom does not prompt that question.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For it is not from wisdom that you ask this.

verses.rationale: Keep inheritance and living-as-sun-seers image.
verses.before: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, and an advantage to people who see the sun.
verses.after: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, an advantage to those who see the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wisdom is good with an inheritance, and an advantage to those who see the sun.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated shade and wisdom’s additional benefit.
verses.before: For wisdom is a shelter, as money is a shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is this: wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.
verses.after: Wisdom offers shade, and money offers shade; but knowledge has this advantage: wisdom keeps its possessors alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: For wisdom is a shelter, as money is a shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is this: wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.

verses.rationale: Keep God’s agency and bent/straight contrast.
verses.before: Consider the work of God: who can straighten what he has made crooked?
verses.after: Look at God’s work. Who can straighten what he has bent?
verses.tsw_comparator: Consider the work of God: who can straighten what he has made crooked?

verses.rationale: Retain adversity’s divine agency and epistemic limit.
verses.before: In a day of prosperity, be in the good; but in a day of adversity, consider: God has made this alongside that, so that no one can discover anything that will come after them.
verses.after: On a good day, enjoy the good; on a bad day, consider: God has made the one as well as the other, so that people cannot discover what comes after them.
verses.tsw_comparator: In a day of prosperity, be in the good; but in a day of adversity, consider: God has made this alongside that, so that no one can discover anything that will come after them.

verses.rationale: Keep moral paradox without rationalizing outcomes.
verses.before: I have seen everything in my days of vapor: there is a righteous person perishing in their righteousness, and there is a wicked person prolonging life in their wickedness.
verses.after: In my breathlike days I have seen everything: a righteous person dying in righteousness, and a wicked person living long in wickedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have seen everything in my days of vapor: there is a righteous person perishing in their righteousness, and there is a wicked person prolonging life in their wickedness.

verses.rationale: Retain provocative excess warning without inserting self-righteousness.
verses.before: Do not be excessively righteous, and do not make yourself overly wise. Why should you bring ruin on yourself?
verses.after: Do not be excessively righteous or make yourself too wise. Why bring ruin on yourself?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be excessively righteous, and do not make yourself overly wise. Why should you bring ruin on yourself?

verses.rationale: Preserve parallel excess and untimely death.
verses.before: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be foolish. Why should you die before your time?
verses.after: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why die before your time?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be foolish. Why should you die before your time?

verses.rationale: Clarify two sayings as referents; note exit idiom.
verses.before: It is good that you hold fast to this and do not let go of that; for the one who fears God will come through them all.
verses.after: It is good to grasp the one warning without letting go of the other. Whoever fears God will come through both.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is good that you hold fast to this and do not let go of that; for the one who fears God will come through them all.

verses.rationale: Preserve ten and comparison to civic power.
verses.before: Wisdom gives strength to the wise more than ten rulers who are in a city.
verses.after: Wisdom makes the wise stronger than ten rulers in a city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wisdom gives strength to the wise more than ten rulers who are in a city.

verses.rationale: Keep universal qualification of righteous conduct.
verses.before: Surely there is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin.
verses.after: There is no righteous person on earth who does good and never sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: Surely there is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin.

verses.rationale: Retain servant and risk of overheard curse.
verses.before: Also, do not take to heart all the things people say, lest you hear your servant cursing you.
verses.after: Do not take to heart every word people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Also, do not take to heart all the things people say, lest you hear your servant cursing you.

verses.rationale: Preserve inward knowledge and reciprocal fault.
verses.before: For your heart knows that you yourself also have often cursed others.
verses.after: Your own heart knows how often you too have cursed others.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your heart knows that you yourself also have often cursed others.

verses.rationale: Keep failed intention and distance metaphor.
verses.before: All this I tested by wisdom. I said, “I will become wise,” but it was far from me.
verses.after: I tested all this by wisdom. I said, “I will become wise,” but wisdom was far from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: All this I tested by wisdom. I said, “I will become wise,” but it was far from me.

verses.rationale: Retain doubled depth and question.
verses.before: What has been is far off, and deep—very deep. Who can find it?
verses.after: What exists is far away, deep, so deep—who can find it?
verses.tsw_comparator: What has been is far off, and deep—very deep. Who can find it?

verses.rationale: Retain deliberate inquiry and layered folly terms.
verses.before: I turned, I and my heart, to know and to search out and seek wisdom and an account, and to know that wickedness is folly and foolishness is madness.
verses.after: I turned my mind to knowing, exploring, and seeking wisdom and an explanation, and to knowing the wickedness of folly and the madness of foolishness.
verses.tsw_comparator: I turned, I and my heart, to know and to search out and seek wisdom and an account, and to know that wickedness is folly and foolishness is madness.

verses.rationale: Preserve gendered claim in speaker’s voice and three trapping images.
verses.before: I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are chains. The one who is good before God escapes her, but the sinner is caught by her.
verses.after: I find more bitter than death the woman who is snares, whose heart is nets and whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is caught by her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are chains. The one who is good before God escapes her, but the sinner is caught by her.

verses.rationale: Keep narrator attribution and unfinished progression into28.
verses.before: “See, this is what I found,” says Qoheleth, “adding one thing to another to find an account,
verses.after: “Look, this is what I found,” says Qohelet, “adding one thing to another to find an explanation—
verses.tsw_comparator: “See, this is what I found,” says Qoheleth, “adding one thing to another to find an account,

verses.rationale: Retain male/female comparison without apologetic addition.
verses.before: which my soul still seeks but has not found: one man among a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find.
verses.after: something I kept seeking but did not find. I found one man among a thousand, but among all these I found no woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: which my soul still seeks but has not found: one man among a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find.

verses.rationale: Retain human collective and upright/schemes contrast.
verses.before: Only see this: I found that God made humanity upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
verses.after: Only this have I found: God made humanity upright, but people have sought many schemes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Only see this: I found that God made humanity upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”

verses.rationale: Keep questions and facial transformation.
verses.before: Who is like the wise person? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A person's wisdom makes their face shine, and the hardness of their face is changed.
verses.after: Who is like the wise? Who knows how to interpret a matter? Wisdom lights up a person’s face and changes its harsh expression.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is like the wise person? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A person's wisdom makes their face shine, and the hardness of their face is changed.

verses.rationale: Supply say for isolated I and retain oath’s divine relation.
verses.before: I say: Keep the king's command, because of the oath of God.
verses.after: I say: obey the king’s command, because of the oath before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: I say: Keep the king's command, because of the oath of God.

verses.rationale: Keep ambiguous bad matter and royal freedom.
verses.before: Do not be hasty to leave his presence. Do not stand in an evil matter, for he does whatever he desires.
verses.after: Do not hurry to leave his presence. Do not persist in a bad cause, for he does whatever he pleases.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be hasty to leave his presence. Do not stand in an evil matter, for he does whatever he desires.

verses.rationale: Retain rhetorical challenge to royal power.
verses.before: For the word of a king is power, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
verses.after: The king’s word carries authority. Who can ask him, “What are you doing?”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the word of a king is power, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”

verses.rationale: Preserve maxim’s absolute form and time/judgment pair.
verses.before: Whoever keeps a command will know no evil thing, and the heart of the wise knows the right time and judgment.
verses.after: Whoever keeps the command will experience no harm; a wise heart knows the proper time and judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever keeps a command will know no evil thing, and the heart of the wise knows the right time and judgment.

verses.rationale: Keep contrast between order and burden.
verses.before: For every matter has its right time and judgment, though the misery of humankind lies heavily upon them.
verses.after: For every matter there is a time and a judgment, though human trouble weighs heavily.
verses.tsw_comparator: For every matter has its right time and judgment, though the misery of humankind lies heavily upon them.

verses.rationale: Retain two distinct future questions.
verses.before: For no one knows what will be; for when it will be, who can tell them?
verses.after: No one knows what will happen. Who can tell how it will happen?
verses.tsw_comparator: For no one knows what will be; for when it will be, who can tell them?

verses.rationale: Keep wind/spirit ambiguity in note and four limits.
verses.before: No one has power over the wind, to restrain the wind; there is no authority on the day of death; there is no discharge in battle; and wickedness will not deliver people who possess it.
verses.after: No one controls the wind so as to hold it back, and no one controls the day of death. There is no discharge in war, and wickedness cannot rescue those who practice it.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one has power over the wind, to restrain the wind; there is no authority on the day of death; there is no discharge in battle; and wickedness will not deliver those who possess it.

verses.rationale: Retain harmful domination and open harm referent.
verses.before: All this I saw, as I gave my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when one person rules over another, to their harm.
verses.after: I saw all this as I applied my heart to every deed done under the sun, at a time when one person rules another to their harm.
verses.tsw_comparator: All this I saw, as I gave my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when one person rules over another, to their harm.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned forgotten rather than silently emend praised.
verses.before: And so I saw the wicked buried. They came and went from the holy place, and they were forgotten in the city where they had done so. This too is vapor.
verses.after: Then I saw wicked people buried. They had come and gone from the holy place, and were forgotten in the city where they had acted that way. This too is breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: And so I saw the wicked buried. They came and went from the holy place, and they were forgotten in the city where they had done so. This too is vapor.

verses.rationale: Keep delayed sentence as cause of emboldening.
verses.before: Because sentence against an evil deed is not carried out swiftly, the hearts of human beings are full of resolve to do evil.
verses.after: When the sentence against an evil deed is not carried out quickly, human hearts become fully bent on doing evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because sentence against an evil deed is not carried out swiftly, the hearts of human beings are full of resolve to do evil.

verses.rationale: Preserve hundred and tension between observation and conviction.
verses.before: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs life, yet I know that it will be well with people who fear God, who fear before him.
verses.after: A sinner may do evil a hundred times and still live long. Yet I also know it will go well with those who fear God, who stand in fear before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs life, yet I know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before him.

verses.rationale: Keep denial in tension with preceding observation.
verses.before: But it will not be well with the wicked, nor will they prolong their days like a shadow, because they do not fear before God.
verses.after: It will not go well with the wicked; they will not lengthen their shadowlike days, because they do not fear God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But it will not be well with the wicked, nor will they prolong their days like a shadow, because they do not fear before God.

verses.rationale: Preserve reversed recompense and doubled hevel.
verses.before: There is a vapor that takes place on the earth: there are righteous people to whom it comes according to the deeds of the wicked, and there are wicked people to whom it comes according to the deeds of the righteous. I said that this too is vapor.
verses.after: There is breath at work on earth: righteous people receive what the wicked deserve, and wicked people receive what the righteous deserve. I said that this too is breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a vapor that takes place on the earth: there are righteous people to whom it comes according to the deeds of the wicked, and there are wicked people to whom it comes according to the deeds of the righteous. I said that this too is vapor.

verses.rationale: Keep bounded enjoyment and accompanying image.
verses.before: So I praised joy, because there is nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat and drink and rejoice. This will accompany them in their toil through the days of their life that God gives them under the sun.
verses.after: So I praised enjoyment. Under the sun, nothing is better for people than to eat, drink, and rejoice. This can accompany them in their work through the days God gives them under the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I praised joy, because there is nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat and drink and rejoice. This will accompany them in their toil through the days of their life that God gives them under the sun.

verses.rationale: Keep sleepless inquiry clause connected to17.
verses.before: When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the task that is done on the earth—even by day and by night one sees no sleep with one's eyes—
verses.after: When I applied my heart to knowing wisdom and observing the activity on earth—even when one’s eyes find no sleep, day or night—
verses.tsw_comparator: When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the task that is done on the earth—even by day and by night one sees no sleep with one's eyes—

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated inability and qualified wise claim.
verses.before: then I saw all the work of God: no one can find out the work that is done under the sun. However much a person labors to seek it, they will not find it; even if the wise claim to know, they cannot find it out.
verses.after: I saw all God’s work: no one can discover the work done under the sun. However hard people search, they cannot find it. Even if the wise claim to know, they cannot discover it.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I saw all the work of God: no one can find out the work that is done under the sun. However much a person labors to seek it, they will not find it; even if the wise claim to know, they cannot find it out.

verses.rationale: Keep divine hand and uncertainty over love/hate without assigning motive.
verses.before: For I have taken all this to heart and examined it all: the righteous, the wise, and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether love or hate, no one knows; everything lies before them.
verses.after: I took all this to heart and examined it: the righteous, the wise, and their deeds are in God’s hand. Whether love or hatred awaits, people do not know; everything lies before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have taken all this to heart and examined it all: the righteous, the wise, and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether love or hate, no one knows; everything lies before them.

verses.rationale: Preserve all named contrasts under shared fate.
verses.before: Everything is the same for everyone: one fate comes to the righteous and the wicked, to the good and the clean and the unclean, to the one who sacrifices and the one who does not sacrifice. As it is with the good, so it is with the sinner; as with the one who swears, so with the one who fears an oath.
verses.after: The same thing comes to everyone: one fate for the righteous and the wicked, the good, the clean and the unclean, those who sacrifice and those who do not. The good fare like sinners; those who swear an oath like those afraid to swear.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everything is the same for everyone: one fate comes to the righteous and the wicked, to the good and the clean and the unclean, to the one who sacrifices and the one who does not sacrifice. As it is with the good, so it is with the sinner; as with the one who swears, so with the one who fears an oath.

verses.rationale: Keep common death and indictment of living hearts.
verses.before: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: one fate comes to everyone. Moreover, the hearts of humankind are full of evil; madness is in their hearts while they live, and afterward—they go to the dead.
verses.after: This is an evil in everything done under the sun: the same fate comes to all. Human hearts are full of evil, and madness fills them while they live. Afterward, they go to the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: one fate comes to everyone. Moreover, the hearts of humankind are full of evil; madness is in their hearts while they live, and afterward—they go to the dead.

verses.rationale: Follow joined read form and retain animal status reversal.
verses.before: For whoever is joined with all the living has hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.after: Anyone still joined to the living has hope: a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.tsw_comparator: For whoever is joined with all the living has hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

verses.rationale: Preserve absolute dead-knowledge statement without harmonizing.
verses.before: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, for their memory is forgotten.
verses.after: The living know they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, for even the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, for their memory is forgotten.

verses.rationale: Retain three passions, finality, and under-sun scope.
verses.before: Their love, their hatred, and their envy have already perished, and they no longer have a share forever in anything that is done under the sun.
verses.after: Their love, hatred, and jealousy have already perished. Never again do they have a portion in anything done under the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their love, their hatred, and their envy have already perished, and they no longer have a share forever in anything that is done under the sun.

verses.rationale: Keep imperative enjoyment and prior acceptance.
verses.before: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already taken pleasure in your works.
verses.after: Go, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already accepted what you do.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already taken pleasure in your works.

verses.rationale: Preserve festive clothing and oil instead of abstract happiness.
verses.before: Let your garments always be white, and do not let oil be lacking on your head.
verses.after: Let your clothes always be white, and never let your head lack oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let your garments always be white, and do not let oil be lacking on your head.

verses.rationale: Retain wife, repeated fleeting days, and portion.
verses.before: Enjoy life with the woman you love, all the days of your vaporous life that God has given you under the sun—all your days of vapor. For this is your portion in life and in your toil at which you labor under the sun.
verses.after: Enjoy life with the wife you love, through all the days of your breathlike life given you under the sun—all your breathlike days. That is your portion in life and in the work you do under the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Enjoy life with the woman you love, all the days of your vaporous life that God has given you under the sun—all your days of vapor. For this is your portion in life and in your toil at which you labor under the sun.

verses.rationale: Retain hand, four absent activities, and Sheol.
verses.before: Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your strength, for there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.
verses.after: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your strength. There is no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your strength, for there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.

verses.rationale: Retain five negated expectations and the time/chance explanation without adding always to the observed reversals.
verses.before: Again I saw under the sun that the race is not for the swift, nor the battle for the strong; nor does bread belong to the wise, nor wealth to those with understanding, nor favor to those with knowledge. For time and chance overtake them all.
verses.after: Again I saw under the sun: the race does not belong to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; bread does not belong to the wise, nor wealth to the discerning, nor favor to the knowledgeable. Time and chance meet them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again I saw under the sun that the race is not for the swift, nor the battle for the strong; nor does bread belong to the wise, nor wealth to those with understanding, nor favor to those with knowledge. For time and chance overtake them all.

verses.rationale: Keep two trapping images and sudden evil time.
verses.before: For no one knows their time. Like fish caught in an evil net, and like birds caught in a trap, so people are snared in an evil time when it falls suddenly upon them.
verses.after: People do not even know their time. Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, they are caught when an evil time suddenly falls on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: For no one knows their time. Like fish caught in an evil net, and like birds caught in a trap, so people are snared in an evil time when it falls suddenly upon them.

verses.rationale: Introduce remembered case with personal assessment.
verses.before: I also saw this example of wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great to me:
verses.after: I also saw this example of wisdom under the sun, and it impressed me greatly:
verses.tsw_comparator: I also saw this example of wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great to me:

verses.rationale: Keep small/few versus powerful/great contrast.
verses.before: There was a small city with few people in it. A great king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siegeworks against it.
verses.after: There was a small city with few people. A powerful king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siegeworks against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a small city with few people in it. A great king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siegeworks against it.

verses.rationale: Keep actual rescue reading and repeated poverty.
verses.before: But there was found in it a poor wise man, and by his wisdom he delivered the city. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
verses.after: A poor, wise man was found there, and he rescued the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
verses.tsw_comparator: But there was found in it a poor wise man, and by his wisdom he delivered the city. Yet no one remembered that poor man.

verses.rationale: Preserve maxim versus social treatment tension.
verses.before: So I said, “Wisdom is better than strength,” yet the wisdom of the poor is despised, and their words are not heard.
verses.after: I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Yet the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and no one listens to his words.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I said, “Wisdom is better than strength,” yet the wisdom of the poor is despised, and their words are not heard.

verses.rationale: Retain the comparative hearing claim and contrast of quiet wisdom with the ruler’s shouting.
verses.before: The words of the wise, spoken quietly, are heard more than the cry of a ruler among fools.
verses.after: Quiet words from the wise are better heard than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of the wise, spoken quietly, are heard more than the cry of a ruler among fools.

verses.rationale: Retain weapons and one-versus-much warning.
verses.before: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
verses.after: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much good.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

verses.rationale: Keep perfume’s corruption and disproportionate folly.
verses.before: Dead flies make the perfumer’s oil stink—make it bubble; so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
verses.after: Dead flies make a perfumer’s oil stink and ferment; a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Dead flies make the perfumer’s oil stink—make it bubble; so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.

verses.rationale: Retain ancient directional image without modern political gloss.
verses.before: The heart of the wise inclines to the right; the heart of the fool, to the left.
verses.after: A wise person’s heart leans right; a fool’s heart leans left.
verses.tsw_comparator: The heart of the wise inclines to the right; the heart of the fool, to the left.

verses.rationale: Read declaration as conduct revealing folly; note alternate speech.
verses.before: Even when the fool walks along the road, his heart is lacking, and he tells everyone, “He is a fool.”
verses.after: Even when a fool walks along the road, he lacks sense and shows everyone he is a fool.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even when the fool walks along the road, his heart is lacking, and he tells everyone, “He is a fool.”

verses.rationale: Preserve rise/rest movement and calm response.
verses.before: If the ruler’s anger rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness puts great offenses to rest.
verses.after: If a ruler’s anger rises against you, do not leave your place. Calmness can lay great offenses to rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the ruler’s anger rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness puts great offenses to rest.

verses.rationale: Keep attribution to ruling mistake.
verses.before: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like an error that goes out from the ruler:
verses.after: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like an error that comes from a ruler:
verses.tsw_comparator: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like an error that goes out from the ruler:

verses.rationale: Retain rich rather than substitute worthy.
verses.before: Folly is set in many high places, while the rich sit in low places.
verses.after: folly is placed in many high positions, while the rich sit low.
verses.tsw_comparator: Folly is set in many high places, while the rich sit in low places.

verses.rationale: Keep class reversal as speaker’s observation.
verses.before: I have seen servants on horses and officials walking on the ground like servants.
verses.after: I have seen slaves on horses and princes walking on the ground like slaves.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have seen servants on horses and officials walking on the ground like servants.

verses.rationale: Retain occupational risks without inventing malicious intention.
verses.before: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a snake.
verses.after: Whoever digs a pit may fall into it; whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a snake.

verses.rationale: Preserve parallel hazardous tasks.
verses.before: Whoever moves stones will be hurt by them; whoever splits logs will be endangered by them.
verses.after: Quarrying stones can injure you; splitting wood can put you in danger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever moves stones will be hurt by them; whoever splits logs will be endangered by them.

verses.rationale: Keep tool/strength relation and wisdom conclusion.
verses.before: If the iron is dull and one does not sharpen its edge, one must use greater strength; but wisdom has the advantage of bringing success.
verses.after: If the iron is blunt and its edge is not sharpened, more strength is needed. Wisdom’s advantage is that it brings success.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the iron is dull and one does not sharpen its edge, one must use greater strength; but wisdom has the advantage of bringing success.

verses.rationale: Retain timing and useless tongue expertise.
verses.before: If a snake bites before it is charmed, there is no advantage for the master of the tongue.
verses.after: If a snake bites before it is charmed, the charmer’s skill brings no advantage.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a snake bites before it is charmed, there is no advantage for the master of the tongue.

verses.rationale: Keep favor versus self-consuming lips.
verses.before: The words from the mouth of the wise are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.
verses.after: Words from a wise mouth bring favor; a fool’s lips swallow him up.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words from the mouth of the wise are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.

verses.rationale: Preserve escalation and beginning/end pair.
verses.before: The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly, and the end of his mouth is wicked madness.
verses.after: His words begin in folly and end in evil madness.
verses.tsw_comparator: The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly, and the end of his mouth is wicked madness.

verses.rationale: Retain excess speech contrasted with unknown future.
verses.before: The fool multiplies words. No one knows what will be; and what will be after him— who can tell him?
verses.after: Yet the fool keeps talking. No one knows what will happen; who can tell anyone what will come afterward?
verses.tsw_comparator: The fool multiplies words. No one knows what will be; and what will be after him— who can tell him?

verses.rationale: Keep concrete inability and exhaustion.
verses.before: The toil of fools wearies them, for they do not know how to go to a city.
verses.after: A fool’s work wears him out; he does not even know the way to town.
verses.tsw_comparator: The toil of fools wearies them, for they do not know how to go to a city.

verses.rationale: Retain boy king and early feast rather than generalized incompetence.
verses.before: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a youth and your officials feast in the morning!
verses.after: How miserable for you, land whose king is a boy and whose princes feast in the morning!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you, O land, when your king is a youth and your officials feast in the morning!

verses.rationale: Keep birth status and meal’s purpose contrast.
verses.before: Happy are you, O land, when your king is a son of nobles and your officials eat at the proper time— for strength, and not for drinking.
verses.after: How fortunate for you, land whose king is nobly born and whose princes eat at the proper time, for strength and not for drunkenness!
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy are you, O land, when your king is a son of nobles and your officials eat at the proper time— for strength, and not for drinking.

verses.rationale: Preserve two maintenance failures and body image.
verses.before: Through laziness the roof sinks in, and through slack hands the house leaks.
verses.after: Through laziness the roof sags; through idle hands the house leaks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through laziness the roof sinks in, and through slack hands the house leaks.

verses.rationale: Keep sweeping money claim without qualification.
verses.before: They make bread for laughter, and wine gladdens life, and money answers everything.
verses.after: A feast is made for laughter, wine makes life glad, and money answers everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: They make bread for laughter, and wine gladdens life, and money answers everything.

verses.rationale: Retain private spaces and repeated avian messengers.
verses.before: Even in your thoughts do not curse a king, and in your bedroom do not curse the rich; for a bird of the air may carry the sound, and a winged creature may tell the matter.
verses.after: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or the rich even in your bedroom. A bird of the sky may carry your voice; a winged creature may report your words.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even in your thoughts do not curse a king, and in your bedroom do not curse the rich; for a bird of the air may carry the sound, and a winged creature may tell the matter.

verses.rationale: Keep concrete bread/water image, leaving explanation to note.
verses.before: Send your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it.
verses.after: Send your bread out over the water; after many days you will find it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Send your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it.

verses.rationale: Preserve escalating numbers and uncertain disaster.
verses.before: Give a portion to seven, even to eight, for you do not know what harm may come upon the earth.
verses.after: Give a portion to seven, even to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come on the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give a portion to seven, even to eight, for you do not know what harm may come upon the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep weather and irreversible fallen-tree images.
verses.before: If clouds are full of rain, they pour it out on the earth; and if a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will remain.
verses.after: If clouds are full of rain, they empty it on the earth. If a tree falls south or north, it stays where it falls.
verses.tsw_comparator: If clouds are full of rain, they pour it out on the earth; and if a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will remain.

verses.rationale: Render habitual watching as impediment to action.
verses.before: Whoever watches the wind will not sow, and whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.
verses.after: Keep watching the wind, and you will never sow; keep looking at the clouds, and you will never reap.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever watches the wind will not sow, and whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.

verses.rationale: Preserve wind/breath ambiguity and prenatal image in note.
verses.before: Just as you do not know the way of the wind, or how bones form in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not know the work of God, who makes everything.
verses.after: You do not know the path of the wind, or how bones take shape in a pregnant woman’s womb. Just so, you do not know the work of God, who makes everything.
verses.tsw_comparator: Just as you do not know the way of the wind, or how bones form in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not know the work of God, who makes everything.

verses.rationale: Keep two times and three possible outcomes.
verses.before: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand rest; for you do not know which will prosper, this or that, or whether both alike will be good.
verses.after: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not let your hand rest in the evening. You do not know which will succeed—this or that, or whether both will do well.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand rest; for you do not know which will prosper, this or that, or whether both alike will be good.

verses.rationale: Retain sensory sweetness and visual good.
verses.before: Sweet is the light, and good for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.after: Light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sweet is the light, and good for the eyes to see the sun.

verses.rationale: Preserve joy alongside long darkness and future hevel.
verses.before: For if a person lives many years, let them rejoice in all of them; but let them remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. All that comes is vapor.
verses.after: If a person lives many years, let them rejoice in them all. But remember the days of darkness, for there will be many. Everything to come is breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if a person lives many years, let them rejoice in all of them; but let them remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. All that comes is vapor.

verses.rationale: Retain male address, permission, and judgment together.
verses.before: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart make you glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and by what your eyes see; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
verses.after: Rejoice, young man, in your youth. Let your heart delight in your young days. Follow your heart’s paths and what your eyes see—but know that for all this God will bring you to judgment.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart make you glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and by what your eyes see; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.

verses.rationale: Keep heart/body and fleeting youth, with dawn ambiguity noted.
verses.before: Remove vexation from your heart, and put away harm from your flesh, for youth and the dawn of life are vapor.
verses.after: Remove vexation from your heart and pain from your body, for youth and the dawn of life are breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remove vexation from your heart, and put away harm from your flesh, for youth and the dawn of life are vapor.

verses.rationale: Preserve Creator imperative and before sequence.
verses.before: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years draw near when you will say, “I have no delight in them”—
verses.after: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days arrive and the years draw near when you say, “I find no pleasure in them”;
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years draw near when you will say, “I have no delight in them”—

verses.rationale: Keep repeated darkness and returning clouds.
verses.before: before the sun and the light grow dark, and the moon and the stars, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.after: before the sun and light grow dark, the moon and stars, and the clouds return after the rain;
verses.tsw_comparator: before the sun and the light grow dark, and the moon and the stars, and the clouds return after the rain;

verses.rationale: Retain human house figures rather than replace them with body parts.
verses.before: on the day when the guards of the house tremble, and the strong men bend themselves, and the women who grind cease because they are few, and people who look through the windows grow dim;
verses.after: when the house’s guards tremble and the strong men bend, the women grinding stop because they are few, and those looking through the windows grow dim;
verses.tsw_comparator: on the day when the guards of the house tremble, and the strong men bend themselves, and the women who grind cease because they are few, and those who look through the windows grow dim;

verses.rationale: Preserve compressed sound imagery and daughters of song.
verses.before: when the doors are shut in the street, as the sound of the mill grows low; when one rises at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song are brought low;
verses.after: when the doors to the street are shut and the mill’s sound fades, when one rises at a bird’s call and all the daughters of song are brought low;
verses.tsw_comparator: when the doors are shut in the street, as the sound of the mill grows low; when one rises at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song are brought low;

verses.rationale: Retain botanical/animal images and death procession without decoding all symbols.
verses.before: when they are afraid of heights, and terrors are in the road; when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper berry fails— for a person goes to their everlasting home, and the mourners circle in the street;
verses.after: when people fear heights and terrors along the road; when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper berry fails— for a person is going to an enduring home, and mourners circle the streets.
verses.tsw_comparator: when they are afraid of heights, and terrors are in the road; when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper berry fails— for a person goes to their everlasting home, and the mourners circle in the street;

verses.rationale: Resume remember from1; follow cord read form and four broken objects.
verses.before: before the silver cord is snapped, and the golden bowl is crushed, and the jar is broken at the spring, and the wheel is crushed at the well;
verses.after: Remember, before the silver cord is snapped, the golden bowl is crushed, the jar is broken at the spring, and the wheel is crushed at the cistern;
verses.tsw_comparator: before the silver cord is snapped, and the golden bowl is crushed, and the jar is broken at the spring, and the wheel is crushed at the well;

verses.rationale: Retain two returns and spirit/breath ambiguity in note.
verses.before: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.after: before the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

verses.rationale: Match opening hevel refrain and narrator’s attribution.
verses.before: “Vapor of vapors,” says the Teacher; “all is vapor.”
verses.after: “Breath of breaths,” says Qohelet. “Everything is breath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Vapor of vapors,” says the Teacher; “all is vapor.”

verses.rationale: Retain three editorial activities and public teaching.
verses.before: Beyond this, because the Teacher was wise, he continually taught the people knowledge. He weighed and searched out and set in order many proverbs.
verses.after: Besides being wise, Qohelet taught the people knowledge. He weighed, investigated, and arranged many proverbs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Beyond this, because the Teacher was wise, he continually taught the people knowledge. He weighed and searched out and set in order many proverbs.

verses.rationale: Keep pleasing speech joined to truthful writing.
verses.before: The Teacher sought to find words of delight, and to write upright words of truth.
verses.after: Qohelet sought words that would give delight, and words of truth written with integrity.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Teacher sought to find words of delight, and to write upright words of truth.

verses.rationale: Keep goads/nails and one shepherd without capitalizing an interpretation.
verses.before: The words of the wise are like goads, and like firmly fixed nails are the masters of collections; they are given by one shepherd.
verses.after: The words of the wise are like goads, and collected sayings like firmly planted nails, given by one shepherd.
verses.tsw_comparator: The words of the wise are like goads, and like firmly fixed nails are the masters of collections; they are given by one shepherd.

verses.rationale: Retain son address and bodily cost of study.
verses.before: And beyond these, my child, be warned: there is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the flesh.
verses.after: Beyond these, my son, be warned: there is no end to making many books, and much study wears out the body.
verses.tsw_comparator: And beyond these, my child, be warned: there is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the flesh.

verses.rationale: Render all-human phrase inclusively, note duty/whole alternative.
verses.before: The end of the matter; all has been heard: fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of humanity.
verses.after: The end of the matter, now that all has been heard: fear God and keep his commandments, for this concerns everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: The end of the matter; all has been heard: fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole of humanity.

verses.rationale: Preserve comprehensive hidden judgment and both moral alternatives.
verses.before: For God will bring every deed into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
verses.after: God will bring every deed into judgment, including every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: For God will bring every deed into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.

comparative_references.scope: All 156 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
